subject: Clarify math on minimums + heartbeat anchoring for long-context sessions
messages:
From: Alex Duarte <alex.duarte@brightserve.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightserve.com
Date: Sun, 03 Dec 2028 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Question on how minimums & heartbeat interact with long sessions

Hi Markus —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. We reviewed the draft SOW and have a couple of accounting questions that need to be clarified for procurement before we sign:

1) If a single user session keeps a 50k token context (long history) but most calls are small incremental messages (10-50 tokens), how are charges computed across the invoice period? Do you bill the full 50k for every request, or is there an amortization/active-window rule?

2) We saw mention of a "heartbeat" to keep KV warm. If we run a 1 request/min heartbeat to keep session latency low, is that considered active usage for minimums or is it excluded/discounted?

3) Rounding: when you apply minimums (e.g., 100 token quantum) how do you round for tiny calls within an active session — always up to the quantum per call or is there session-level aggregation?

Attaching the SOW and a simple invoice template we asked our finance team to prepare. Procurement is cc'd. Would appreciate a concise explanation we can show them.

Best,
Alex
Alex Duarte
Director of Data Products
BrightServe

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alex Duarte <alex.duarte@brightserve.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 Dec 2028 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on how minimums & heartbeat interact with long sessions

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by worked examples in the next message (we'll attach a sample invoice):

1) We do NOT bill the full 50k for every single request. Billing is a mix of per-call tokens and a short active-window aggregation. The long context itself only contributes to the bill when it is read/ streamed back or affects generation tokens.

2) Heartbeat traffic is considered "activity" for session-level minimums if it comes from a client-initiated request that consumes inference compute (i.e., it triggers KV access). We can exclude dedicated keep-alive pings that hit a lightweight API path (no KV) if you prefer — that is a common carve-out for enterprise pilots.

3) Rounding is by quantum per invoice line item, but we apply session aggregation across a rolling hour window for small calls to avoid gross up on micro-calls. That said, minimums are applied at the SKU level (e.g., streaming generation minimum 1,000 tokens/month) unless you opt into a seat/commit model.

Vanessa and Tessa, looping you in to confirm the exact wording we can include in the SOW. Alex — I will follow with two concrete math examples showing the rounding and heartbeat behavior.

Thanks,
Markus
VP, Pricing & GTM Economics
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alex Duarte <alex.duarte@brightserve.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 05 Dec 2028 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on how minimums & heartbeat interact with long sessions — worked examples

Alex —

Worked examples (numbers intentionally simple):

Scenario A — long context read, small response calls
- Context size: 50,000 tokens stored (no charge for storage by itself).
- Call: user sends 20-token delta, model returns 40 tokens. To generate the 40 tokens, the runtime reads KV cache for the relevant context blocks. Billing steps:
  • Input tokens: 20 (billed per-call)
  • Output tokens: 40 (billed per-call)
  • Context read cost: we bill a context-read delta equivalent to the tokens streamed from the KV into the generation path — in practice this is only the subset used for attention (not the entire 50k every time).
  • Rounding quantum: per-call token billed = round_up(20+40+context_read, quantum). If the quantum is 100 tokens, that call becomes 100 tokens billed.

Scenario B — heartbeat to keep session warm (1/min)
- Heartbeat payload: lightweight request that confirms KV presence but doesn't run full generation (no output tokens).
  • Default policy: heartbeat counted as minimal compute call and aggregated into the session's hourly bucket. If within an hour the aggregated calls sum to < quantum, we roll them up to the quantum once per hour rather than billing each minute.
  • Enterprise carve-out: if BrightServe wants heartbeats excluded entirely, we can classify them as "keepalive" (no KV touch) and not count them toward minimums. That requires a small SDK flag and an addendum in the SOW.

Scenario C — monthly minimums and invoice-flooring
- Example: streaming generation SKU has a 10k token monthly minimum (commit). If total billed tokens across invoice items fall below 10k, you'll get charged up to 10k for that SKU. We apply invoice-level credits for ephemeral test traffic and can carve out authenticated heartbeat tokens if contractually agreed.

Attached: a sample invoice showing the rounding math across 12 small calls and the hourly aggregation on heartbeats.

Ben — can you confirm the exact quantum we should put in the SOW (our standard is 100 tokens, but we can set a custom quantum for pilots)?

Markus

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Alex Duarte <alex.duarte@brightserve.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 05 Dec 2028 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on how minimums & heartbeat interact with long sessions — quantum confirmation

Markus / Alex —

Confirming our standard quantum is 100 tokens for hosted streaming & generation SKUs. A couple of practical notes:

- For calls where (input+output+context_read) < quantum, we aggregate per session on a rolling one-hour window and bill the rounded-up quantum once per hour. That prevents 60x multipliers from minute-level heartbeats.
- If a customer wants per-request rounding (no aggregation) we can enable that, but it tends to increase bill unpredictably for high-heartbeat patterns.
- For Dedicated/Dedicated-Private contracts we can set a smaller quantum (e.g., 20 tokens) as part of the reserved capacity pricing.

Alex — if you want heartbeats excluded, Tessa can draft the addendum language and Vanessa will confirm any pricing delta.

Ben
Principal Pricing Analyst
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Question on how minimums & heartbeat interact with long sessions — SOW language + next steps

Alex —

Thanks for raising this. For procurement, here's a concise paragraph we can include in the SOW. You can paste it into your packet:

"Billing mechanics: Charges are based on tokens consumed by requests and responses plus any context read necessary to produce output. Token billing is subject to a per-SKU quantum (standard 100 tokens) and monthly invoice minimums as specified in Section 4.2. To avoid excessive billing from keepalive traffic, Redwood applies a rolling hourly aggregation for sub-quantum calls; enterprise customers may opt to classify SDK keepalive calls as "non-billable keepalives" via an agreed addendum. Dedicated capacity customers can negotiate different quanta and minimums."

Next steps:
- If BrightServe wants keepalives excluded, sign the addendum I will draft (small one-time engineering flag + contract clause).
- If you want a different quantum for the pilot, tell us target (20/50/100) and we will price it in the SOW.

I'll attach a redline of the SOW with the paragraph and the addendum stub once you confirm.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
